key_insight: CARing improves next-visit diagnosis prediction by representing diagnoses as compact semantic tokens and training with coverage-aware rewards so the model covers more correct diagnoses instead of repeating the same ones.
clinical_relevance: This could help clinical NLP systems better support multi-label diagnosis prediction from longitudinal EHRs, especially when several diagnoses are valid at the same time.
method: Encodes ontology-enriched disease semantics into compositional Semantic IDs (SIDs) via residual quantization.
Aligns SID tokens with natural language and longitudinal EHR context using multi-task alignment and reasoning-enriched training.
Uses coverage reward plus multi-positive supervision, with inference via constrained decoding or multi-chain reasoning with rank fusion.
evidence_signal: On MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV, the method outperformed EHR-trained baselines in weighted F1 and achieved the best top-k recall at all reported cutoffs, including R@30 of 46.04% and 46.52% in reasoning mode.
watch_item: Because the approach relies on ontology mapping, SID construction, and constrained reasoning pipelines, performance may depend on high-quality coding infrastructure and may be less portable to settings with different vocabularies or incomplete EHR text.
paper_title: Coverage-Aware Reasoning with Medical Tokens for Diagnosis Prediction
